<user_query>
Continue the Channel Intelligence Platform (CIP) programme and begin production
implementation of the accepted N-0013 r3/r3.1 North Star.

CIP repo:
C:\Users\warren_eliason\channel-intelligence-platform

Expected branch:
feat/ns-2-brief-nav-collapse

EIF repo:
C:\AI\engineering-intelligence-framework

CIP and EIF are separate repositories. Work on CIP only. Do not modify EIF.
If EIF causes real implementation friction, record it for the later EIF repair
session rather than fixing EIF here.

============================================================
1. OPERATOR DECISIONS — RECORD FIRST
============================================================

Perform the minimum read-only repository checks first:
- confirm repository;
- branch;
- commit;
- git status;
- unexpected uncommitted work.

Then this message gives explicit operator authority to record:

- D-0008: ACCEPTED — N-0013 r3/r3.1 design direction.
  D-0007 remains superseded.

- N-0013: ACCEPTED / COMPLETE using the programme ledger's existing valid
  vocabulary — architecture/design gate satisfied by r3/r3.1 and independent
  GOV-008 verification.

- D-0009 remains OPEN / PROPOSED.
  It concerns disposition of the rejected N-0010 "Actions / ranked commercial
  actions" framing. Do not resolve it.

- D-0002 remains OPEN / DEFERRED.
  Do not resolve it.

N-0010 is NOT the Promotion Planner, Plan Templates, or Promotions & Funding.

Show the resulting programme state and evidence the writes succeeded.

If the programme control plane cannot represent or authorise the requested
D-0008/N-0013 state, stop and report the exact issue rather than bypassing it.

============================================================
2. ACCEPTED PRODUCT DIRECTION
============================================================

The design phase is complete. Do NOT reopen architecture or generate alternative
IA concepts.

Accepted primary domains:

Overview
- Business Dashboard
- Attention
- Reports

Stock & Sell-through
- Cover
- Movement
- Sell-through
- Execution vs plan
- Forecasts

Supply & Inbound
- Shipments
- Receipts & POD
- PO coverage

Planning
- Lineup cases
- Readiness
- Line economics
- PO reconciliation
- Rankings
- related product-roadmap/planning capability where supported

Promotions & Funding
- Promotion Planner
- Case Book
- Claims evidence
- Payments
- Plan Templates
- Terms & assumptions
- Budget Ledger according to its truthful implementation maturity

Market & Listings
- Monitored listings
- Price history
- Promotion activation
- Feed proposals
- Competitor mappings
- Competitor prices
- Competitor listings
- Listing quality / SEO

Data & Stewardship
- Import Center
- Steward queue
- Products
- Customers
- Distributors
- Steward audit

Administration
- Users & roles
- Operations
- SQL viewer
- Audit log
- Settings

Also accepted:
- configurable Business Dashboard;
- Attention distinct from Dashboard;
- Reports as governed questions/reports, pinnable to Dashboard;
- command/search palette;
- capability directory;
- product/customer/case context drawers and cross-workflow links;
- preserve useful existing workflow density and functionality.

Do not return to:
Brief · Plan · Position · Settlement · Actions · Imports.

============================================================
3. CRITICAL PRODUCT RULES
============================================================

PROMOTIONS

A promotion plan and its later funding/settlement case are the same canonical
object:

cpor_case / cpor_case_line

Do not create a second promotion-plan model.

The Promotion Planner is a real authoring workflow, not merely history or
monitoring.

Reuse real existing planner/case capability and evolve it toward the accepted
r3.1 workspace.

PLAN TEMPLATES

Canonical CIP data is truth.

Customer workbooks are external formats.

Direction:
external template ↔ canonical CIP model

The intended architecture is map-once/reuse for import and export, with
direction-aware rules. Reuse/evolve CanonicalColumnMappingPanel where suitable.

Do not hard-code one customer's workbook as product law.

MARKET & LISTINGS

This is a reusable evidence domain, not a sub-feature of Promotion Planner.

Competition means:
our SKU ↔ competing SKU

not customer-vs-customer.

Do not fabricate uplift, elasticity, market share, causality, impact or
confidence where the governed data does not support it.

CAPABILITY MATURITY

Keep:
live · partial · substrate/data-only · planned

truthful.

Do not promote substrate/planned functionality merely because it appears in
the North Star.

============================================================
4. IMPLEMENTATION, NOT REDESIGN
============================================================

Do not restart product discovery.

However, implementation reconciliation IS required.

For each implementation slice determine:

- what production route exists;
- what component exists;
- what API/service/model exists;
- what should be reused;
- what should be evolved;
- what should eventually be retired;
- how the accepted design-lab evidence maps onto the real product.

The design-lab is design evidence, not a second application.

Do not copy fixture-driven screens into production and leave the old workflow
beside them indefinitely.

Use real application data and business logic.

Preserve useful existing:
- filters;
- grids;
- tables;
- drawers;
- forms;
- selectors;
- states;
- evidence;
- workflow depth.

Do not remove capability merely for visual minimalism.

============================================================
5. DESIGN LANGUAGE V2
============================================================

Create only the minimum normative v2 baseline necessary for implementation.

Do not spend the run writing a large design-system document.

v2 must come from the accepted React prototype, strong existing CIP components
and production implementation — not screenshots alone.

Normative rule:

A successful reference composition is NOT a mandatory page anatomy.

"KPI cards + chart + right panel" is not a CIP page template.

Each domain may use the grids, tables, editors, forms, charts, worklists,
drawers, evidence panels, timelines or other composition appropriate to its job.

============================================================
6. IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY RULES
============================================================

Do not big-bang rewrite.

Use coherent vertical slices and leave the application operational.

Important invariants:

- one governed calculation/result for the same canonical fact;
- explanation/provenance must reproduce the result it claims to explain;
- product/customer/case context must not leak across entities;
- scoped workflow links should preserve relevant scope across the destination;
- permissions/partner scope must prevent unauthorised data;
- tenant/customer fixture assumptions must not become reusable product law;
- deprecated prototype APIs should not be propagated into new production code.

Known design-lab inconsistencies are implementation acceptance criteria when
their affected capability is reached, not a reason for another design audit.

For example:
- list/detail promotion totals must agree;
- competitor score explanation must reproduce the actual score;
- OfficeWorld must not use TechMart evidence;
- stale N-0010 copy must disappear;
- maturity/navigation state must remain truthful.

============================================================
7. DATA / MIGRATION SAFETY
============================================================

The database contains real data.

Before any database write, positively confirm the database being targeted.
Do not assume environment variables are safe.

Never run destructive tests against the development/production data store.

Schema changes must be justified by an actual implementation gap.

Prefer additive migrations.

Test migrations on a safe clone first with database identity and relevant
before/after counts.

Any migration that drops, rewrites or destructively changes existing data
requires operator approval before touching the real database.

Do not combine a schema migration and dependent product UI into one opaque
commit.

Do not reset, clean or discard existing repository work.

Use explicit git staging paths; do not use git add -A.

============================================================
8. START THE MIGRATION
============================================================

After recording the operator decisions:

A. Establish current production state relevant to migration.

B. Build a concise dependency map:
- what shared foundation must come first;
- what existing production capability already satisfies the North Star;
- what can migrate independently;
- where duplicate work/schema/permission risks exist.

C. Choose the first vertical implementation slice from actual dependency
evidence.

Do NOT choose purely by navigation order.

Do NOT manufacture multiple options unless two genuinely consequential
strategies exist.

For the first slice report briefly:

- product job/business rule;
- current production implementation;
- accepted target;
- code/components/APIs/models to reuse;
- exact delta;
- tests;
- production rendered verification;
- way back if the slice fails;
- explicit non-goals.

Then, unless a genuine operator decision is required:

BEGIN IMPLEMENTATION.

Do not stop after producing another audit/planning document.

============================================================
9. PER-SLICE COMPLETION
============================================================

For each coherent slice:

- implement;
- test;
- render the actual production route;
- exercise important interactions/states;
- verify responsive/permission/scope behaviour where relevant;
- report changed files and test results;
- identify legacy paths retained for safe migration;
- record genuine EIF friction for later;
- proceed to the next logical slice.

Do not self-promote authored evidence into independent PASS.

Verification asks:

"Did we implement the accepted target correctly?"

not:

"Should we redesign the product again?"

============================================================
CORE PRINCIPLE
============================================================

The design phase is over.

Make the real product become the accepted product.

Reuse what is already good.
Replace what is genuinely wrong.
Preserve business logic and useful workflow depth.
Use real data.
Do not let prototype fixtures become product law.
Do not let the old architecture survive permanently beside the new one.
Do not redesign what has already been decided.

Implement.
</user_query>
I'll start with the required session orientation and a read-only git check, then record the operator decisions before any implementation.
Memory palace is current: N-0013 is still blocked pending D-0008. Next I’ll confirm git state and how the programme ledger records those decisions.
